{"path": "t4-writ/test/queue/core_spec.clj", "content": "(ns queue.core-spec
  "The contract for queue.core: jobs with priorities, leases and retries.

  Time is a Nat tick the caller passes; nothing reads a clock.  A lease is
  live while `now < :until`.  The job taken next is the due `:ready` job of
  the highest priority, then the earliest `:ready-at`, then the lowest id.
  A job that fails while leased comes back `2^attempts` ticks later, and a
  job of 3 or more attempts dies instead."
  (:require [writ.spec :refer [spec ann law graph refine example]]))

(spec queue.core)

;; --- the data --------------------------------------------------------------

(defn job-shape?
  "Leases go with `:leased`, and only with `:leased`."
  [j]
  (case (:status j)
    :leased (some? (:lease j))
    (:ready :done :dead) (nil? (:lease j))
    false))

(defn settled-job [j]
  (cond
    (= :leased (:status j)) (assoc j :lease (if (map? (:lease j)) (:lease j) {:worker 0 :until 0}))
    (contains? #{:ready :done :dead} (:status j)) (assoc j :lease nil)
    :else (assoc j :status :ready :lease nil)))

(refine Job [j {:id Nat, :priority Nat, :attempts Nat, :status Keyword,
                :ready-at Nat, :lease (Opt {:worker Nat, :until Nat})}]
  (job-shape? j)
  {:build settled-job})

(defn keyed?
  "Every job sits under its own id, below the next id to hand out."
  [q]
  (every? (fn [k] (< k (:next-id q))) (keys (:jobs q))))

(defn settled [q]
  (let [jobs (into {} (map-indexed (fn [i j] [i (assoc j :id i)]) (vals (:jobs q))))]
    {:jobs jobs :next-id (+ (count jobs) (:next-id q))}))

(refine Queue [q {:jobs (Index :id Job), :next-id Nat}]
  (keyed? q)
  {:build settled})

;; --- the order -------------------------------------------------------------

(defn due? [j now] (and (= :ready (:status j)) (<= (:ready-at j) now)))

(defn outranks? [a b]
  (or (> (:priority a) (:priority b))
      (and (= (:priority a) (:priority b))
           (or (< (:ready-at a) (:ready-at b))
               (and (= (:ready-at a) (:ready-at b)) (< (:id a) (:id b)))))))

(defn live? [j now] (and (= :leased (:status j)) (< now (:until (:lease j)))))

(defn backoff [n] (case n 0 1 1 2 2 4 0))

(defn reaped
  "The job after it fails: dead at 3 attempts, else ready again, 2^attempts
  ticks on, in either case with no lease."
  [j now]
  (if (>= (:attempts j) 3)
    (assoc j :status :dead :lease nil)
    (assoc j :status :ready :ready-at (+ now (backoff (:attempts j))) :lease nil)))

(defn may-act?
  "The job is leased, to this worker, on a live lease."
  [j worker now]
  (and (some? j) (= :leased (:status j)) (= worker (:worker (:lease j)))
       (< now (:until (:lease j)))))

;; --- signatures ------------------------------------------------------------

(ann enqueue  [Queue Nat Nat -> (Tuple Queue Nat)])
(ann next-job [Queue Nat -> (Opt Nat)])
(ann lease    [Queue Nat Nat -> (Tuple Queue (Opt Nat))])
(ann complete [Queue Nat Nat Nat -> Queue])
(ann fail     [Queue Nat Nat Nat -> Queue])
(ann expire   [Queue Nat -> Queue])

;; --- the state graph -------------------------------------------------------

(graph queue
  {:start  [:q {:jobs {} :next-id 0}]
   :states {:q Queue
            :enq (Tuple Queue Nat)
            :lea (Tuple Queue (Opt Nat))
            :id (Opt Nat)}
   :edges  {:q {[enqueue Nat Nat] #{:enq}
                [next-job Nat] #{:id}
                [lease Nat Nat] #{:lea}
                [complete Nat Nat Nat] #{:q}
                [fail Nat Nat Nat] #{:q}
                [expire Nat] #{:q}}
            :enq {[first] #{:q}}
            :lea {[first] #{:q}}}
   :final  [:id]})

;; --- what each step means --------------------------------------------------

(law enqueue-adds-the-next-job
  (forall [q Queue, priority Nat, now Nat]
    (let [[q' id] (enqueue q priority now)
          j (get (:jobs q') id)]
      (and (= id (:next-id q))
           (= (inc (:next-id q)) (:next-id q'))
           (= (:jobs q) (dissoc (:jobs q') id))
           (= priority (:priority j))
           (= 0 (:attempts j))
           (= :ready (:status j))
           (= now (:ready-at j))
           (= nil (:lease j))))))

(law next-job-is-nil-exactly-when-nothing-is-due
  (forall [q Queue, now Nat]
    (= (nil? (next-job q now))
       (not (some (fn [j] (due? j now)) (vals (:jobs q)))))))

(law the-next-job-is-due
  (forall [q Queue, now Nat]
    (let [id (next-job q now)]
      (=> (some? id) (due? (get (:jobs q) id) now)))))

(law nothing-due-outranks-the-next-job
  (forall [q Queue, now Nat]
    (let [id (next-job q now)]
      (=> (some? id)
          (every? (fn [k] (=> (due? (get (:jobs q) k) now)
                              (not (outranks? (get (:jobs q) k) (get (:jobs q) id)))))
                  (keys (:jobs q)))))))

(law lease-takes-the-next-job
  (forall [q Queue, worker Nat, now Nat]
    (let [[q' id] (lease q worker now)
          want (next-job q now)]
      (and (= want id)
           (if (nil? want)
             (= q' q)
             (let [j (get (:jobs q) want)]
               (= q' (assoc q :jobs
                            (assoc (:jobs q) want
                                   (assoc j :status :leased
                                          :attempts (inc (:attempts j))
                                          :lease {:worker worker :until (+ now 10)})))))))))))

(law complete-finishes-a-live-lease
  (forall [q Queue, id Nat, worker Nat, now Nat]
    (let [j (get (:jobs q) id)]
      (= (complete q id worker now)
         (if (may-act? j worker now)
           (assoc q :jobs (assoc (:jobs q) id (assoc j :status :done :lease nil)))
           q)))))

(law fail-retries-and-then-kills
  (forall [q Queue, id Nat, worker Nat, now Nat]
    (let [j (get (:jobs q) id)]
      (= (fail q id worker now)
         (if (may-act? j worker now)
           (assoc q :jobs (assoc (:jobs q) id (reaped j now)))
           q)))))

(law expire-reaps-any-lease-that-has-run-out
  (forall [q Queue, now Nat]
    (= (expire q now)
       (assoc q :jobs
              (into {} (for [[k j] (:jobs q)]
                         [k (if (and (= :leased (:status j))
                                     (<= (:until (:lease j)) now))
                              (reaped j now)
                              j)]))))))

;; --- the boundaries and ties, named ----------------------------------------

(example enqueue
  [{:jobs {} :next-id 0} 7 3]
  [{:jobs {0 {:id 0 :priority 7 :attempts 0 :status :ready :ready-at 3 :lease nil}}}
   0])

(example next-job
  [{:jobs {0 {:id 0 :priority 5 :attempts 0 :status :ready :ready-at 1 :lease nil}
           1 {:id 1 :priority 5 :attempts 0 :status :ready :ready-at 1 :lease nil}
           2 {:id 2 :priority 9 :attempts 0 :status :ready :ready-at 4 :lease nil}}
    :next-id 3}
   5]
  2)

(example next-job
  [{:jobs {0 {:id 0 :priority 5 :attempts 0 :status :ready :ready-at 3 :lease nil}
           1 {:id 1 :priority 5 :attempts 0 :status :ready :ready-at 1 :lease nil}}
    :next-id 2}
   5]
  1)

(example next-job
  [{:jobs {0 {:id 0 :priority 5 :attempts 0 :status :ready :ready-at 0 :lease nil}
           1 {:id 1 :priority 5 :attempts 0 :status :ready :ready-at 0 :lease nil}}
    :next-id 2}
   0]
  0)

(example next-job
  [{:jobs {0 {:id 0 :priority 5 :attempts 0 :status :ready :ready-at 7 :lease nil}}
    :next-id 1}
   7]
  0)

(example next-job
  [{:jobs {0 {:id 0 :priority 5 :attempts 0 :status :ready :ready-at 8 :lease nil}}
    :next-id 1}
   7]
  nil)

(example next-job
  [{:jobs {0 {:id 0 :priority 99 :attempts 1 :status :leased :ready-at 0
              :lease {:worker 2 :until 100}}
           1 {:id 1 :priority 1 :attempts 0 :status :ready :ready-at 0 :lease nil}}
    :next-id 2}
   5]
  1)

(example next-job

           1 {:id 1 :priority 1 :attempts 0 :status :dead :ready-at 0 :lease nil}}
    :next-id 2}

(example lease

    :next-id 1}

  (let [ks (map f xs)] (= (count ks) (count (distinct ks)))))

(defn indexed?
  "Is db a map of records, each kept under its field k, no two sharing a
  field named in unique?  What an (Index :k R :unique [...]) says beyond
  its records' own type; a refinement of an Index checks it in its
  predicate, so a step that lands in one must keep it."
  [k unique db]
  (and (map? db)
       (every? (fn [[i x]] (= i (get x k))) db)
       (every? #(unique-by? % (vals db)) unique)))

(defn- refinement [t tenv]
  (when (symbol? t) (get-in tenv [::refines (symbol (name t))])))

(def ^:private conformers
  "Each type's compiled check, by type, for the few type environments
  seen last, each found by identity: a check runs the code thousands of
  times, every value through the same few types."
  (atom []))

(declare conformer)

(defn- conformer*
  "Type t compiled to a predicate on values under tenv: what conforms?
  says of a value, the type read once."
  [t tenv]
  (let [t (plain t)
        c #(conformer % tenv)]
    (cond
      (refinement t tenv)
      (let [{:keys [base pred]} (refinement t tenv)
            base? (c base)]
        (fn [v] (boolean (and (base? v) (pred v)))))

      (symbol? t)
      (case t
        Nat nat-int?
        Int int?
        Bool boolean?
        String string?
        Char char?
        Keyword keyword?
        Symbol symbol?
        (Float Double Float! Double!) number?
        Unit nil?
        (Any Any!) (constantly true)
        (if-let [[d args] (data-decl t tenv)]
          (fn [v] (conforms-data? d args v tenv))
          (constantly true)))

      ;; a record: each key of its own type; an (Opt T) key may be absent,
      ;; and keys it does not name may be there too
      (map? t)
      (let [ks (mapv (fn [[k kt]] [k (c kt) (opt-type? kt)]) t)]
        (fn [v] (and (map? v)
                     (every? (fn [[k ok? opt]] (if (contains? v k) (ok? (get v k)) opt)) ks))))

      (and (kind/index-type? t) (not (data-decl t tenv)))
      (let [{k :key r :of u :unique} (kind/index-parts t)
            r? (c r)]
        (fn [v] (and (map? v)
                     (every? (fn [[i x]] (and (r? x) (= i (get x k)))) v)
                     (every? #(unique-by? % (vals v)) u))))

      (seq? t)
      (let [[h & as] t
            a? (delay (c (first as)))]
        (case h
          Opt (fn [v] (or (nil? v) (@a? v)))
          List (fn [v] (and (or (nil? v) (sequential? v)) (every? @a? v)))
          Vec (fn [v] (and (vector? v) (every? @a? v)))
          Set (fn [v] (and (set? v) (every? @a? v)))
          Map (let [b? (delay (c (second as)))]
                (fn [v] (and (map? v) (every? (fn [[k x]] (and (@a? k) (@b? x))) v))))
          (Tuple &) (let [cs (delay (mapv c as))]
                      (fn [v] (and (vector? v) (= (count as) (count v))
                                   (every? true? (map #(%1 %2) @cs v)))))
          -> ifn?
          (if-let [[d args] (data-decl t tenv)]
            (fn [v] (conforms-data? d args v tenv))
            (constantly true))))

      :else (constantly true))))

  "Type t's compiled check under tenv, compiled once."
  [t tenv]

[f xs]
  (let [ks (map f xs)] (= (count ks) (count (distinct ks)))))

(defn indexed?
  "Is db a map of records, each kept under its field k, no two sharing a
  field named in unique?  What an (Index :k R :unique [...]) says beyond
  its records' own type; a refinement of an Index checks it in its
  predicate, so a step that lands in one must keep it."
  [k unique db]
  (and (map? db)
       (every? (fn [[i x]] (= i (get x k))) db)
       (every? #(unique-by? % (vals db)) unique)))

(defn- refinement [t tenv]
  (when (symbol? t) (get-in tenv [::refines (symbol (name t))])))

(def ^:private conformers
  "Each type's compiled check, by type, for the few type environments
  seen last, each found by identity: a check runs the code thousands of
  times, every value through the same few types."
  (atom []))

(declare conformer)

(defn- conformer*
  "Type t compiled to a predicate on values under tenv: what conforms?
  says of a value, the type read once."
  [t tenv]
  (let [t (plain t)
        c #(conformer % tenv)]
    (cond
      (refinement t tenv)
      (let [{:keys [base pred]} (refinement t tenv)
            base? (c base)]
        (fn [v] (boolean (and (base? v) (pred v)))))

      (symbol? t)
      (case t
        Nat nat-int?
        Int int?
        Bool boolean?
        String string?
        Char char?
        Keyword keyword?
        Symbol symbol?
        (Float Double Float! Double!) number?
        Unit nil?
        (Any Any!) (constantly true)
        (if-let [[d args] (data-decl t tenv)]
          (fn [v] (conforms-data? d args v tenv))
          (constantly true)))

      ;; a record: each key of its own type; an (Opt T) key may be absent,
      ;; and keys it does not name may be there too
      (map? t)
      (let [ks (mapv (fn [[k kt]] [k (c kt) (opt-type? kt)]) t)]
        (fn [v] (and (map? v)
                     (every? (fn [[k ok? opt]] (if (contains? v k) (ok? (get v k)) opt)) ks))))

      (and (kind/index-type? t) (not (data-decl t tenv)))
      (let [{k :key r :of u :unique} (kind/index-parts t)
            r? (c r)]
        (fn [v] (and (map? v)
                     (every? (fn [[i x]] (and (r? x) (= i (get x k)))) v)
                     (every? #(unique-by? % (vals v)) u))))

      (seq? t)
      (let [[h & as] t
            a? (delay (c (first as)))]
        (case h
          Opt (fn [v] (or (nil? v) (@a? v)))
          List (fn [v] (and (or (nil? v) (sequential? v)) (every? @a? v)))
          Vec (fn [v] (and (vector? v) (every? @a? v)))
          Set (fn [v] (and (set? v) (every? @a? v)))
          Map (let [b? (delay (c (second as)))]
                (fn [v] (and (map? v) (every? (fn [[k x]] (and (@a? k) (@b? x))) v))))
          (Tuple &) (let [cs (delay (mapv c as))]
                      (fn [v] (and (vector? v) (= (count as) (count v))
                                   (every? true? (map #(%1 %2) @cs v)))))
          -> ifn?
          (if-let [[d args] (data-decl t tenv)]
            (fn [v] (conforms-data? d args v tenv))
            (constantly true))))

      :else (constantly true))))

(defn- conformer
  "Type t's compiled check under tenv, compiled once."
  [t tenv]
  (let [cs @conformers
        [_ m] (or (some #(when (identical? tenv (first %)) %) cs)
                  (let [e [tenv (atom {})]]
                    (swap! conformers #(conj (if (< (count %) 8) % (subvec % 1)) e))
                    e))]
    (or (get @m t)
        (let [f (conformer* t tenv)]
          (swap! m assoc t f)
          f))))

(defn conforms?

(ns dispatch.core-spec
  "The contract for dispatch.core: a tick of the clock hands due jobs to
  workers through the queue.

  A tick first expires the queue at `now`, then walks the workers in order:
  a worker that already holds a live lease gets nothing, any other leases
  the next job if there is one.  The assignments come back in the order
  they were leased, so the same worker listed twice leases at most one job.
  The queue's own laws are taken from queue.core-spec and are not restated
  here."
  (:require [writ.spec :refer [spec ann law graph example calls]]))

(spec dispatch.core {:uses [queue.core-spec]})

;; --- the queue, in this spec's own words -----------------------------------

(defn due? [j now] (and (= :ready (:status j)) (<= (:ready-at j) now)))

(defn live-lease? [q w now]
  (some (fn [j] (and (= :leased (:status j))
                     (= w (:worker (:lease j)))
                     (< now (:until (:lease j)))))
        (vals (:jobs q))))

(defn backoff [n] (case n 0 1 1 2 2 4 0))

(defn reaped [j now]
  (if (>= (:attempts j) 3)
    (assoc j :status :dead :lease nil)
    (assoc j :status :ready :ready-at (+ now (backoff (:attempts j))) :lease nil)))

(defn expired [j now]
  (if (and (= :leased (:status j)) (<= (:until (:lease j)) now))
    (reaped j now)
    j))

(defn outranks? [a b]
  (or (> (:priority a) (:priority b))
      (and (= (:priority a) (:priority b))
           (or (< (:ready-at a) (:ready-at b))
               (and (= (:ready-at a) (:ready-at b)) (< (:id a) (:id b)))))))

(defn pick [q now]
  (let [cands (filter (fn [j] (due? j now)) (vals (:jobs q)))]
    (when (seq cands)
      (:id (first (sort-by (fn [j] [(- (:priority j)) (:ready-at j) (:id j)]) cands))))))

(defn lease-one [q w now]
  (if-let [id (pick q now)]
    (let [j (get (:jobs q) id)]
      [(assoc q :jobs
              (assoc (:jobs q) id
                     (assoc j :status :leased
                            :attempts (inc (:attempts j))
                            :lease {:worker w :until (+ now 10)})))
       id])
    [q nil]))

(defn assign [q workers now]
  (reduce (fn [[q as] w]
            (if (live-lease? q w now)
              [q as]
              (let [[q2 id] (lease-one q w now)]
                [q2 (if (some? id) (conj as [w id]) as)])))
          [q []]
          workers))

(defn model-tick
  "The tick, said here: expire, then lease in worker order, skipping any
  worker who already holds a live lease."
  [q workers now]
  (assign (assoc q :jobs (into {} (for [[k j] (:jobs q)] [k (expired j now)])))
          workers now))

;; --- signatures ------------------------------------------------------------

(ann tick    [Queue (Vec Nat) Nat -> (Tuple Queue (Vec (Tuple Nat Nat)))])
(ann backlog [Queue Nat -> Nat])

;; --- the state graph -------------------------------------------------------

(graph dispatch
  {:start  [:q {:jobs {} :next-id 0}]
   :states {:q Queue
            :ticked (Tuple Queue (Vec (Tuple Nat Nat)))
            :n Nat}
   :edges  {:q {[tick (Vec Nat) Nat] #{:ticked}
                [backlog Nat] #{:n}}
            :ticked {[first] #{:q}}}
   :final  [:n]})

;; --- how it is put together ------------------------------------------------

(calls tick [queue.core/expire queue.core/lease])
(calls backlog [])

;; --- what each step means --------------------------------------------------

(law a-tick-expires-first-and-then-hands-out-jobs
  (forall [q Queue, workers (Vec Nat), now Nat]
    (= (tick q workers now) (model-tick q workers now))))

(law backlog-counts-the-due-ready-jobs
  (forall [q Queue, now Nat]
    (= (backlog q now)
       (count (filter (fn [j] (due? j now)) (vals (:jobs q)))))))

(law every-assignment-is-a-lease-to-that-worker
  (forall [q Queue, workers (Vec Nat), now Nat]
    (let [[q' as] (tick q workers now)]
      (every? (fn [[w id]]
                (let [j (get (:jobs q') id)]
                  (and (= :leased (:status j))
                       (= w (:worker (:lease j)))
                       (= (+ now 10) (:until (:lease j))))))
              as))))

(law one-assignment-per-worker
  (forall [q Queue, workers (Vec Nat), now Nat]
    (let [[_ as] (tick q workers now)]
      (= (count as) (count (distinct (map first as)))))))

(law a-worker-holding-a-live-lease-gets-nothing

    (=> (live-lease? q w now)

{"content": "(ns dispatch.core-spec
  "The contract for dispatch.core: a tick of the clock hands due jobs to
  workers through the queue.

  A tick first expires the queue at `now`, then walks the workers in order:
  a worker that already holds a live lease gets nothing, any other leases
  the next job if there is one.  The assignments come back in the order
  they were leased, so the same worker listed twice leases at most one job.
  The queue's own laws are taken from queue.core-spec and are not restated
  here."
  (:require [writ.spec :refer [spec ann law graph example calls]]))

(spec dispatch.core {:uses [queue.core-spec]})

;; --- the queue, in this spec's own words -----------------------------------

(defn due? [j now] (and (= :ready (:status j)) (<= (:ready-at j) now)))

(defn live-lease? [q w now]
  (some (fn [j] (and (= :leased (:status j))
                     (= w (:worker (:lease j)))
                     (< now (:until (:lease j)))))
        (vals (:jobs q))))

(defn backoff [n] (case n 0 1 1 2 2 4 0))

(defn reaped [j now]
  (if (>= (:attempts j) 3)
    (assoc j :status :dead :lease nil)
    (assoc j :status :ready :ready-at (+ now (backoff (:attempts j))) :lease nil)))

(defn expired [j now]
  (if (and (= :leased (:status j)) (<= (:until (:lease j)) now))
    (reaped j now)
    j))

(defn outranks? [a b]
  (or (> (:priority a) (:priority b))
      (and (= (:priority a) (:priority b))
           (or (< (:ready-at a) (:ready-at b))
               (and (= (:ready-at a) (:ready-at b)) (< (:id a) (:id b)))))))

(defn pick [q now]
  (let [cands (filter (fn [j] (due? j now)) (vals (:jobs q)))]
    (when (seq cands)
      (:id (first (sort-by (fn [j] [(- (:priority j)) (:ready-at j) (:id j)]) cands))))))

(defn lease-one [q w now]
  (if-let [id (pick q now)]
    (let [j (get (:jobs q) id)]
      [(assoc q :jobs
              (assoc (:jobs q) id
                     (assoc j :status :leased
                            :attempts (inc (:attempts j))
                            :lease {:worker w :until (+ now 10)})))
       id])
    [q nil]))

(defn assign [q workers now]
  (reduce (fn [[q as] w]
            (if (live-lease? q w now)
              [q as]
              (let [[q2 id] (lease-one q w now)]
                [q2 (if (some? id) (conj as [w id]) as)])))
          [q []]
          workers))

(defn model-tick
  "The tick, said here: expire, then lease in worker order, skipping any
  worker who already holds a live lease."
  [q workers now]
  (assign (assoc q :jobs (into {} (for [[k j] (:jobs q)] [k (expired j now)])))
          workers now))

;; --- signatures ------------------------------------------------------------

(ann tick    [Queue (Vec Nat) Nat -> (Tuple Queue (Vec (Tuple Nat Nat)))])
(ann backlog [Queue Nat -> Nat])

;; --- the state graph -------------------------------------------------------

(graph dispatch
  {:start  [:q {:jobs {} :next-id 0}]
   :states {:q Queue
            :ticked (Tuple Queue (Vec (Tuple Nat Nat)))
            :n Nat}
   :edges  {:q {[tick (Vec Nat) Nat] #{:ticked}
                [backlog Nat] #{:n}}
            :ticked {[first] #{:q}}}
   :final  [:n]})

;; --- how it is put together ------------------------------------------------

(calls tick [queue.core/expire queue.core/lease])
(calls backlog [])

;; --- what each step means --------------------------------------------------

(law a-tick-expires-first-and-then-hands-out-jobs
  (forall [q Queue, workers (Vec Nat), now Nat]
    (= (tick q workers now) (model-tick q workers now))))

(law backlog-counts-the-due-ready-jobs
  (forall [q Queue, now Nat]
    (= (backlog q now)
       (count (filter (fn [j] (due? j now)) (vals (:jobs q)))))))

(law every-assignment-is-a-lease-to-that-worker
  (forall [q Queue, workers (Vec Nat), now Nat]
    (let [[q' as] (tick q workers now)]
      (every? (fn [[w id]]
                (let [j (get (:jobs q') id)]
                  (and (= :leased (:status j))
                       (= w (:worker (:lease j)))
                       (= (+ now 10) (:until (:lease j))))))
              as))))

(law one-assignment-per-worker
  (forall [q Queue, workers (Vec Nat), now Nat]
    (let [[_ as] (tick q workers now)]
      (= (count as) (count (distinct (map first as)))))))

(law a-worker-holding-a-live-lease-gets-nothing
  (forall [q Queue, w Nat, workers (Vec Nat), now Nat]
    (=> (live-lease? q w now)
        (let [[_ as] (tick q workers now)]
          (not (some (fn [[x _]] (= x w)) as))))))

;; --- the boundaries, named -------------------------------------------------

(example backlog
  [{:jobs {0 {:id 0 :priority 5 :attempts 0 :status :ready :ready-at 7 :lease nil}}
    :next-id 1}
   7]
  1)

(example backlog

    :next-id 1}

import re, pathlib
root = pathlib.Path('.')
q = (root/'src/queue/core.clj').read_text()
d = (root/'src/dispatch/core.clj').read_text()

def qmut(name, old, new, count=1):
    t = q.replace(old, new, count)
    assert t != q, (name, old)
    t = t.replace('(ns queue.core', '(ns queue.'+name, 1)
    (root/f'src/queue/{name}.clj').write_text(t)

def dmut(name, old, new, count=1):
    t = d.replace(old, new, count)
    assert t != d, (name, old)
    t = t.replace('(ns dispatch.core', '(ns dispatch.'+name, 1)
    (root/f'src/dispatch/{name}.clj').write_text(t)

# Q2 lease until now+9
qmut('mq_lease9', ':until (+ now 10)', ':until (+ now 9)')
# Q3 complete counts now=until live
qmut('mq_complete_lte', '(< now (:until (:lease j)))', '(<= now (:until (:lease j)))', 1)
# Q4 fail kills only above 3
qmut('mq_fail_gt3', '(>= (:attempts j) 3)', '(> (:attempts j) 3)')
# Q5 expire does not reap at until=now
qmut('mq_expire_lt', '(<= (:until (:lease j)) now)', '(< (:until (:lease j)) now)')
# Q7 wrong backoff for second attempt
qmut('mq_backoff', '(case n 0 1 1 2 2 4 0)', '(case n 0 1 1 2 2 9 0)')
# Q8 enqueue does not advance next-id
qmut('mq_nextid', ':next-id (inc id)', ':next-id id')
# Q9a complete ignores who holds the lease
qmut('mq_complete_worker', '             (= worker (:worker (:lease j)))\n             (< now (:until (:lease j))))\n      (assoc q :jobs (assoc (:jobs q) id (assoc j :status :done :lease nil)))',
     '             (< now (:until (:lease j))))\n      (assoc q :jobs (assoc (:jobs q) id (assoc j :status :done :lease nil)))')
# Q9b next-job ignores status (takes any job)
qmut('mq_status', '  (let [cands (filter (fn [j] (due? j now)) (vals (:jobs q)))]',
     '  (let [cands (filter (fn [j] (<= (:ready-at j) now)) (vals (:jobs q)))]')

# D1 tick does not expire first
dmut('md_noexpire', 'let [expired (queue/expire q now)', 'let [expired q')
# D2 tick walks workers in reverse
dmut('md_reverse', '                  [expired []]\n                  workers)]', '                  [expired []]\n                  (reverse workers))]')
# D3 tick does not skip a worker who holds a live lease
dmut('md_noskip', '(if (some (fn [j]\n                                (and (= :leased (:status j))\n                                     (= w (:worker (:lease j)))\n                                     (< now (:until (:lease j)))))\n                              (vals (:jobs q)))\n                      [q acc]\n                      (let [[q2 id] (queue/lease q w now)]\n                        [q2 (if (some? id) (conj acc [w id]) acc)])))',
     '(let [[q2 id] (queue/lease q w now)]\n                        [q2 (if (some? id) (conj acc [w id]) acc)]))')
# D4 backlog excludes ready-at = now
dmut('md_backlog_lt', '(<= (:ready-at j) now)))', '(< (:ready-at j) now)))')
print("mutants written")
PY

# Notes on the spec

Two namespaces, two writ specs. `bin/check` exits 0. Both specs are
checked with `{:require :proved}`; where the prover cannot reach a law it
is marked `{:require :tested :because "…"}`, and the two graph steps whose
obligations are only tested carry `:tested {[state f] "…"}`.

## The one spec change after the `specs` commit

The specs were committed before any implementation, as asked. Once the
code existed and the check passed, I strengthened the spec-level default
from "may be proved or tested" to `{:require :proved}` and named, with a
`:because`, each law the prover cannot prove. No law's statement, no
`ann`, no refinement and no `:require` on the component changed; the
contract is the one that was committed. The change only *asks* for proof
where the prover can give it and records honestly where it cannot:

- queue: `next-job-is-nil-exactly-when-nothing-is-due` (the `filter` over
  the map's values), `the-next-job-is-due` and
  `nothing-due-outranks-the-next-job` (the `sort-by` ranking),
  `lease-takes-the-next-job` (the whole-queue comparison behind that
  ranking), `expire-reaps-any-lease-that-has-run-out` (its `for`/`into`
  model), and the two graph steps `queue:q:lease.first` and
  `queue:q:expire` (the same two reasons).
- dispatch: the tick model, the assignment-vector laws and the
  live-lease law (all read through the `reduce` the prover leaves
  opaque), and the graph step `dispatch:q:tick.first`.

Before settling on it I checked the spec against twelve deliberately
broken implementations (wrong tie-break, `now+9` lease, `<=` on lease
liveness, `>3` death threshold, `now+8` backoff, a non-advancing
`next-id`, a status-blind `next-job`, a worker-blind `complete`, a tick
that forgets to expire, walks workers backwards, never skips a live-lease
holder, or counts backlog with `<`). Every one failed the check, most on
the law that states that very rule.

## What was hard to say in the spec

**Well-formed queues are built, not found.** TASK gives a queue as
`{:jobs {id job}, :next-id Nat}`. For the laws to be about jobs that
really are the queue's jobs, the spec's `Queue` refinement asks that each
job sits under its own `:id` (`(Index :id Job)`) and that `:next-id` is
above every id. A random record almost never meets that, so `Queue` has
`:build settled`, which renumbers a generated queue's jobs `0,1,2,…` and
sets `:next-id` above them. That builder is generation only; it is not
part of the contract, and it is why the same queue a law sees may have
different ids from the one drawn.

**TASK never says key = job's `:id`; the spec decides it does.** The
`(Index :id Job)` field is a reading of `{id job}`: the map's key *is* the
job's identity. A queue whose keys and `:id`s disagree is not a value of
`Queue` here. `enqueue`'s law even relies on it: `(= (:jobs q) (dissoc
(:jobs q') id))` says the new job is added, not swapped for an old one,
which is only true when `:next-id` was fresh.

**"fails, as `fail` says" cannot call `fail`.** `fail` fires only on a
*live* lease, and `expire` fires exactly on leases that are *no longer*
live. So the spec restates the transition once as `reaped` and uses it in
both `fail` and `expire`; the two share one definition of dying and
retrying (`2^attempts`, dead at 3). That paraphrase is the one place the
contract is not passed straight to the code.

**A workflow cannot be its own model, so the dispatcher is modelled in
the spec's own words.** The dispatch spec builds on the queue spec, but a
spec helper may not call the component — otherwise the workflow would be
judged by the very code it builds on. `model-tick` therefore repeats, in
dispatch.core-spec's own names, what expire and the lease-selection do,
and the tick law equates the code with it. The repetition is the price of
stating tick's whole behaviour (`expire` first, workers in order, skip a
live-lease holder, at most one lease per worker, assignments in lease
order) in one law; the smaller tick laws restate the pieces and are the
ones a reader should look at.

**The tie-break laws need examples to be sure.** `nothing-due-outranks-
the-next-job` is a strict total order — priority down, `:ready-at` up,
`:id` up — and it pins `next-job` completely, but random queues rarely
make two due jobs tie on all three keys. The three `example`s that make
each tie are what actually exercise it; mutation testing shows the tie
law catches a reversed tie-break anyway, because its `every?` checks
every pair on every trial.

**The dispatch `calls` is exact, so it is also a contract on structure.**
`(calls tick [queue.core/expire queue.core/lease])` says a tick goes
*through* the queue, and inlining the lease selection fails it even if
every law holds. It does not constrain how tick checks for a worker's
live lease: it may read the queue's jobs directly.

## What the report's notes mean

- `` `backoff`: (clojure.core/= n 2) was never false `` (and the same
  note for `queue.core/backoff` in the dispatch report) is about dead
  code, not a gap: `reaped` calls `backoff` only under `(< attempts 3)`,
  so the `case`'s test for `2` is only ever reached when `n` is 2, and its
  default arm is never taken. No law can try the other way because the
  code cannot reach it.
- `` `a-worker-holding-a-live-lease-gets-nothing` is thinly tested ``
  names a real rarity — a randomly generated queue seldom holds a *live*
  lease for the very worker being considered. The two tick `example`s
  where a worker does hold one pin the case, and the tick model law covers
  it too. The same law, and its two companion assignment laws, "tell none
  of tick's stand-ins" on their own; together with the model law they
  reject every impostor `tick` is tested against.

## What I could not express

- That `expire`'s reaping and `fail`'s reaping are the *same* operation
  is said by sharing `reaped`, but TASK's phrase "fails, as fail says" is
  not itself checkable; only the resulting values are.
- That "the same worker listed twice leases at most one job" is a
  *consequence* of a worker holding a live lease after its first lease is
  not expressed; it is stated as its own law (`one-assignment-per-worker`)
  and by the model.
- The prover has no model of `sort-by`, of a `filter` over a map's values,
  of `for`/`into`, or of a `reduce` over the workers, so those laws are
  tested (hundreds of inputs each, plus named examples) rather than
  proved. Their `:because` strings say so in every report.
- Nothing reads a clock and nothing effects anything, so there was nothing
  to say about time beyond passing `now` in; the specs sign no clock.

## Files

- `test/queue/core_spec.clj` constrains `src/queue/core.clj`.
- `test/dispatch/core_spec.clj` constrains `src/dispatch/core.clj` and
  builds on the queue spec with `:uses [queue.core-spec]`.

`bin/check` exits 0. Here's the summary.

## What I did

**Stage 1 — specs (committed as `specs`, before any implementation):**
- `test/queue/core_spec.clj` — constrains `queue.core`. Refines `Job` (status/lease agree) and `Queue` (every job under its own id, `:next-id` above them), signs all six fns, and states: `enqueue` adds exactly the next job; `next-job` is nil exactly when nothing is due and no due job outranks its pick (priority, then earliest `:ready-at`, then lowest id); `lease` takes that job and gives it `{:until now+10}` with `attempts+1`; `complete`/`fail`/`expire` as whole-queue equalities; `fail` retries at `2^attempts` and dies at 3. Eighteen examples name every boundary and tie: `ready-at = now`, `until = now`, attempts 2 vs 3, the three tie-breaks, wrong worker, leased/done/dead excluded from the pick.
- `test/dispatch/core_spec.clj` — builds on the queue spec with `:uses [queue.core-spec]`. Its strong law equates `tick` with a model of the whole tick (expire first, workers in order, skip a live-lease holder, one lease per worker, assignments in lease order); `backlog` counts due `:ready` jobs. `calls` says `tick` goes exactly through `queue.core/expire` and `queue.core/lease`. Examples name the boundaries and ordering.

**Stage 2 — implementations:** `src/queue/core.clj` and `src/dispatch/core.clj`.

## Spec change made after the `specs` commit (and why)

I raised the spec-level default to `{:require :proved}` and added a `:because` to each law the prover cannot reach (the `sort-by` ranking laws, the `for`/`into` expire model, and the `reduce`-built dispatch laws), plus `:tested {[state f] "…"}` on the two graph steps. **No law statement, `ann`, refinement, or component `:require` changed** — this only asks for proof where possible and records honestly where it isn't.

## Validation

I mutation-tested the spec against 12 broken implementations (reversed tie-break, `now+9` lease, `<=` lease liveness, `>3` death threshold, `now+8` backoff, non-advancing `next-id`, status-blind `next-job`, worker-blind `complete`, tick that forgets to expire / walks backwards / never skips a live-lease holder, and `<` backlog). Every one failed the check.

## Notes on the report

The only "tests no law took both ways" note is `` `backoff`: (= n 2) was never false `` — dead code, since `reaped` calls `backoff` only under `(< attempts 3)`, so the `case`'s default arm is unreachable. The thinly-tested live-lease law is rare in random queues but is pinned by examples and the tick model. Details, plus what was hard to say in the spec, are in `NOTES.md`.
